transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Evan Chu (Redwood CSM); Dana Lee, Michael O'Connor, Sofia Reyes, Jamal Price (StrataCare)

Auto Summary (auto-generated may be rough):
- Focus on compliance items for pilot; SSO flows mostly good but SCIM mapping needs tweak.
- Audit log retention default 90 days; customer asking for 365-day option and SIEM export.
- Discussed SOC2 evidence process and what Redwood can surface.
- Performance: 95th p50 latency ~220ms w/o SSO, up to ~420ms with SSO token exchange; Priya to run bench with SSO token caching.

[00:00] Alex Rivera: ok hey team, thanks for taking time today, um, this is our weekly checkpoint for the StrataCare pilot, focusing on the compliance items you flagged last week. quick roll call, then we can jump in.
[00:18] Dana Lee: thanks Alex, Dana here. we'll mostly be listening in and Michael will walk through security reqs.
[00:27] Michael O'Connor: yep hi all, Michael. I've got the SOC2 matrix open, and a few questions on log contents.
[00:33] Priya Desai: great, hi Michael, quick note — we tested the SAML integration and SCIM last night and saw one mapping mismatch where groups were not populated, probably around the lowercase/uppercase claim name, will share details.
[00:44] Jamal Price: thx Priya. also, we found that the pilot VM cannot reach one of your ingestion endpoints because our outbound egress is locked down.
[00:52] Alex Rivera: thanks Jamie — we'll capture that as an action. Priya, can you give a short result overview from the last 48 hours?
[01:00] Priya Desai: sure. so on the POC metrics, overall throughput is in line with expectations. for the 6k token test we saw average token time about 8.5ms, p50 end-to-end generation 210 to 240ms when using hosted auth. when we add SSO SAML exchange on the client side the p95 moves to ~420ms because of repeated token handshakes in our test harness. important note: once we enable token caching the p95 drops to ~270ms — so caching helps a ton. also observed a handful of 503s during a synthetic spike where batch sizes were 32, we think that's hitting an instance scaling boundary.
[01:35] Michael O'Connor: are those 503s visible in audit logs, like do we get request IDs? our security team needs request-level correlation for incident response.
[01:41] Priya Desai: yes, every request has a request_id that shows in the audit stream, plus user_id and route, and a model_variant field. we'll drop a sample log with anonymized PII.
[01:52] Sofia Reyes: can we see the retention window for those logs? StrataCare needs 365 days for a subset of logs for compliance.
[01:58] Alex Rivera: default retention is 90 days in hosted, but we support extended retention as an add-on or via forwarding logs to your SIEM. two options: 1) Redwood retains extended retention under contract, we can do 365; 2) forward via syslog/CloudWatch/Loki to your tenant, you control retention.
[02:15] Michael O'Connor: forwarding is preferable, but we also need a short-term store for quick audits. is there an export API?
[02:22] Priya Desai: yes, there's an export API and also continuous forwarders. export API is paged and supports time-range queries and the log schema is JSON. continuous forwarders can push to your AWS account or a collector with TLS mutual auth.
[02:33] Jamal Price: noted — we'll need firewall IPs and cert pins for the collector.
[02:38] Alex Rivera: will provide firewall ranges and cert thumbprints in a follow-up doc.
[02:42] [03:01] Michael O'Connor: quick SOC2 question — what evidence artifacts can Redwood provide? for example, access logs, change control, patch windows, and encryption key rotation records.
[03:10] Evan Chu: we can surface the usual artifacts: access logs, admin activity logs, role-based access change events, and KMS rotation metadata. For rotation we store rotation timestamps and the KMS key alias used; if you need HSM attestations we can coordinate through our enterprise channel.
[03:26] Dana Lee: ok so for the pilot we just need the admin actions and login traces for the service accounts that we pointed at. also, would you be able to redact PII? we don't want user emails in logs.
[03:36] Priya Desai: we can mask or hash emails in the log stream; the export API supports field-filtering. by default we omit full prompt text from long-term logs — short transients include prompt hashes for QA correlation.
[03:48] Sofia Reyes: that's helpful. what's the deletion / data retention process when the pilot ends? StrataCare needs guaranteed deletion on termination plus a certificate.
[03:55] Alex Rivera: standard process: we can run a data purge job that deletes prompts, embeddings, and related KV cache for your tenant, and then produce an attestation of deletion. for hosted we typically have a 30-day grace period but for pilot customers we can accelerate and provide a deletion certificate within 7 business days after termination per agreement.
[04:12] Michael O'Connor: do you also purge backups? we have to show backups were also removed.
[04:17] Priya Desai: backups are registrable — we can remove snapshot copies and include snapshot IDs in the attestation. that's part of the enterprise flow.
[04:25] [05:05] Dana Lee: circling back on SSO, we ran a full sign-on test and SCIM provisioning. group mapping failed for a subset; Michael and Priya, can you triage the claim mapping?
[05:17] Michael O'Connor: yes, my team captured logs showing an attribute called "groups" sent as an array versus expected comma-separated string; SCIM mapping in your dashboard expects the latter, can that be adjusted?
[05:27] Priya Desai: we can map both formats; update the mapping rule in the tenant config. I'll push a small roll with the mapping and confirm.
[05:34] Jamal Price: fyi the SSO flow also touches your token service endpoint — if we enable token caching, what's the TTL and how do we revoke tokens?
[05:43] Alex Rivera: token TTL is configurable; for pilots we default to 1 hour but you can set shorter TTL and we support immediate revocation via admin portal or API which returns a revocation confirmation event into the audit stream.
[05:55] [06:15] Priya Desai: on the performance note: when we enable token caching on the client side (so you do the SAML exchange once and keep a session token), we saw latency improvements and the overall token ops dropped by 85%. will include bench artifacts.
[06:30] Michael O'Connor: any crypto details we should know? encryption at rest and in-transit? KMS vs HSM?
[06:36] Evan Chu: in transit is TLS 1.2+, and at rest we use AES-256 with customer-managed keys option. for enterprise customers we offer KMS integration with your cloud provider or our HSM-backed key manager. rotation logs are available for audit.
[06:50] Sofia Reyes: what's the story for EU residency? some of our data must stay in EU.
[06:55] Alex Rivera: we support region pinning; your tenant can be provisioned into the eu-west region and logs + data remain there. note: some control-plane metadata may still be in our control plane; we can provide documentation on what lives where.
[07:08] [08:00] Dana Lee: ok good. one more item — incident response. if there's a suspected data exfil, what timeline and artifacts do you provide?
[08:10] Priya Desai: we provide request-level logs, timeline of admin actions, and any model variant changes; we can also give a timeline of autoscaling events. turnaround depends on severity, but for pilot customers we commit to a 48-hour initial packet, and enterprise SLAs can tighten that.
[08:25] Michael O'Connor: for the POC we need a 48-hour initial response and the ability to pull raw audit logs on-demand. is that possible?
[08:32] Alex Rivera: yes, we'll include access to a read-only export role so you can pull raw logs for investigations.
[08:38] [09:15] Sofia Reyes: switching briefly to the POC results: Priya you mentioned failed 503s with large batch sizes — what's the recommendation?
[09:24] Priya Desai: recommended immediate mitigation is to cap client batch size to 16 and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. long term options: reserved capacity or vertical scaling for the model. also testing a quantized 8-bit variant reduced memory pressure in our tests with similar output quality on your workloads.
[09:42] Jamal Price: curious if quantization affects our quality checks — we run evals against clinical prompts.
[09:47] Priya Desai: we can run a small regressions eval set against the 8-bit variant and report ROUGE/ BLEU-like metrics and sample outputs.
[09:55] [10:01] Alex Rivera: ok we'll add that to the action items — Priya to run quantization regressions.
[10:06] Michael O'Connor: getting back to logs schema, we need a sample with field definitions — request_id, user_id, route, model_variant, latency_ms, http_status, and a correlation_id for cross-system tracing.
[10:18] Priya Desai: yes we'll share the log schema and a sanitized sample. correlation_id is present and ties into our tracing headers.
[10:26] Dana Lee: also can you include the admin change event schema and a mapping to SOC2 control IDs?
[10:32] Evan Chu: we'll map those events to the SOC2 categories in a matrix and share it.
[10:38] [11:03] Michael O'Connor: final compliance Q — are you SOC2 Type II certified? what's the most recent audit date?
[11:09] Alex Rivera: yes, Redwood achieved SOC2 Type II; last audit completed Q2 2025. we can provide the report under an NDA and can set up a redacted copy for your security team.
[11:22] Sofia Reyes: great. last thing — pilot pricing impact if we enable 365-day retention on Redwood side?
[11:29] Alex Rivera: there's a modest per-GB/month add-on for extended retention; I'll include numbers in the dedicated worksheet. forwarding to your SIEM is typically cheaper if you already pay for storage there.
[11:40] [12:00] Priya Desai: quick note on SSO quirks — one of our test identities triggered a rate limit during provisioning; we can relax SCIM rate limits for your tenant during pilot.
[12:09] Jamal Price: appreciated. that will help.
[12:13] [13:00] Alex Rivera: ok let's recap next steps: Alex sends pricing + pilot usage spreadsheet, Priya runs SSO-enabled bench and quantization regressions and shares logs/schema, Michael will send SOC2 matrix and retention policy, Jamal checks firewall rules and returns egress list, we schedule a SIEM export deep-dive. any other items?
[13:30] Michael O'Connor: no, that's it. thanks.
[13:33] Dana Lee: thanks everyone.
[13:36] Alex Rivera: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with artifacts.

End of transcript.

- Sample audit log schema (to be sent by Priya)
